description: Which sync session wins, hand-written x2 (native shells only). `hostedConnectEntry` says what a hosted connect does about a session already in hand — skip the wizard's idempotent re-entry, replace a live self-hosted one, or proceed (D8). `restoreBranch` says which credential a cold launch reaches for, including the one stranded device that holds both (D9). Justin's calls of 2026-09-16, specified once in docs/spec/sync.md.
note: LOCKED: both consumers read the full shared fixture — Swift's SyncSessionModeConformanceTests.swift and Kotlin's SyncSessionModeConformanceTest.kt each assert all 8 hostedConnectEntry and all 4 restoreBranch cases, and both assert the case counts first so a truncated fixture fails rather than passing vacuously. Desktop has NO copy on purpose: it holds ONE engine session and `SyncSession::connect_hosted` stops the previous live loop itself, so there is no teardown to sequence and `ensureConnected` already prefers hosted — a Swift/Kotlin-shaped copy there would be drift, not parity.
